raw_findings.body: react-i18next will not substitute `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` nor evaluate the `choice` clause, so end users will see the literal raw string '...{0}...{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.' instead of a properly pluralized, substituted error message.
raw_findings.evidence: error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.
raw_findings.failure_mode: User-facing error text renders unresolved template syntax instead of the intended human-readable message.
raw_findings.impact: react-i18next will not substitute `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` nor evaluate the `choice` clause, so end users will see the literal raw string '...{0}...{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.' instead of a properly pluralized, substituted error message.
raw_findings.root_cause: The Java-theme (FreeMarker/MessageFormat) wording convention for this key was copied into the react-i18next resource bundle without adapting the placeholder/pluralization syntax to the framework actually consuming this file.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Revert to the double-brace i18next placeholder convention used elsewhere in this file (e.g. `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`) or use an i18next-supported pluralization mechanism (e.g. `_one`/`_other` keys) instead of a Java MessageFormat choice clause.
raw_findings.title: React i18next placeholder replaced with Java MessageFormat choice syntax breaks account-ui message interpolation
raw_findings.trigger: The account-ui React app renders the multivalued attribute size error using react-i18next, which interpolates using the `{{param}}` double-brace convention used by every other key in this same file (e.g. `{{0}}`, `{{username}}`); this key now uses single-brace Java MessageFormat placeholders plus an embedded `{2,choice,...}` clause.

raw_findings.body: The unchecked RuntimeException propagates out of verify() uncaught, so callers (e.g. ThemeVerifierMojo) receive a raw RuntimeException/stack trace instead of the documented MojoExecutionException, breaking the expected error-handling contract of verify() and producing a less controlled build failure.
raw_findings.evidence:
} catch (IOException e) {
            throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + file, e);
raw_findings.failure_mode: Uncontrolled exception type escapes the public verify() API, degrading error diagnostics and violating the method's declared exception contract.
raw_findings.impact: The unchecked RuntimeException propagates out of verify() uncaught, so callers (e.g. ThemeVerifierMojo) receive a raw RuntimeException/stack trace instead of the documented MojoExecutionException, breaking the expected error-handling contract of verify() and producing a less controlled build failure.
raw_findings.root_cause: New verifySafeHtml() method converts checked IOException into an unchecked RuntimeException instead of integrating with the existing checked-exception flow used by verify().
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Let verifySafeHtml() declare 'throws IOException' (or otherwise propagate the checked exception) so it is caught by the existing try/catch(IOException) in verify() and converted into a MojoExecutionException, consistent with verifyNoDuplicateKeys().
raw_findings.title: verifySafeHtml() wraps missing-file IOException as unchecked RuntimeException, bypassing verify()'s error handling contract
raw_findings.trigger: When either the target properties file or its derived English sibling file cannot be opened (e.g. missing/renamed English source file, permission issue) during verifySafeHtml(), which is invoked from verify() inside a try block that only catches checked IOException.

raw_findings.body: A regression that causes verifySafeHtml() to falsely flag legitimate translations (e.g. an identical anchor tag or an allowed element like <b>/<strong> matching the English source) as illegal HTML would not be caught by the current test suite, silently breaking valid theme builds.
raw_findings.failure_mode: False-positive regressions in the HTML sanitizer logic would go undetected by the test suite.
raw_findings.impact: A regression that causes verifySafeHtml() to falsely flag legitimate translations (e.g. an identical anchor tag or an allowed element like <b>/<strong> matching the English source) as illegal HTML would not be caught by the current test suite, silently breaking valid theme builds.
raw_findings.root_cause: New sanitizer test coverage only exercises the negative (violation-detected) branches of verifySafeHtml(), omitting the positive (no-violation) acceptance path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a fixture pair (e.g. matching *_en.properties / *_xx.properties with identical allowed tags/anchors) and a test asserting VerifyMessageProperties.verify() returns an empty list for that case.
raw_findings.title: No positive-path test verifying that legitimate translations with matching allowed HTML pass without false-positive errors
raw_findings.trigger: All four newly added tests (verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected, verifyNoHtmlAllowed, verifyNoChangedAnchors, plus the duplicate-key test) only assert that an offending message IS produced; none assert that a valid translation reusing the same allowed elements/anchors as the English source produces an EMPTY message list.

validated_findings.trigger: The account-ui React app renders the multivalued attribute size error using react-i18next, which interpolates using the `{{param}}` double-brace convention used by every other key in this same file (e.g. `{{0}}`, `{{username}}`); this key now uses single-brace Java MessageFormat placeholders plus an embedded `{2,choice,...}` clause.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch changes the key in messages_en.properties, but the repository context shows normalizeValue() at line 124 explicitly handles 'error-invalid-multivalued-size' by replacing the choice clause with '...'. This is intentional handling for the theme-verifier, and the file is under maven-resources (not maven-resources-community), indicating it's the English source file processed by Java MessageFormat, not react-i18next. The claim that react-i18next consumes this file is ungrounded.

validated_findings.body: react-i18next will not substitute `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` nor evaluate the `choice` clause, so admins will see the literal raw string instead of a properly pluralized, substituted error message when editing user-profile attribute validators.
validated_findings.evidence: error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.
validated_findings.failure_mode: User-facing error text renders unresolved template syntax instead of the intended human-readable message.
validated_findings.impact: react-i18next will not substitute `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` nor evaluate the `choice` clause, so admins will see the literal raw string instead of a properly pluralized, substituted error message when editing user-profile attribute validators.
validated_findings.root_cause: The Java-theme (FreeMarker/MessageFormat) wording convention for this key was copied into the react-i18next resource bundle without adapting the placeholder/pluralization syntax to the framework actually consuming this file.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Revert to the double-brace i18next placeholder convention (e.g. `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`) or replace the Java choice clause with an i18next-supported pluralization key.
validated_findings.title: React i18next placeholder replaced with Java MessageFormat choice syntax breaks admin-ui message interpolation
validated_findings.trigger: The admin-ui React app renders the multivalued attribute size error using react-i18next, which interpolates using the `{{param}}` double-brace convention used elsewhere in this file; this key now uses single-brace Java MessageFormat placeholders plus an embedded `{2,choice,...}` clause.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Same as candidate 0: the admin-ui messages_en.properties file is under maven-resources (not maven-resources-community), and the normalizeValue() method explicitly handles this key. The claim that react-i18next directly consumes this English source file is ungrounded - it's a Java MessageFormat source file.

validated_findings.body: The unchecked RuntimeException propagates out of verify() uncaught, so callers (e.g. ThemeVerifierMojo) receive a raw RuntimeException/stack trace instead of the documented MojoExecutionException, breaking the expected error-handling contract of verify() and producing a less controlled build failure.
validated_findings.evidence:
} catch (IOException e) {
            throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + file, e);
validated_findings.failure_mode: Uncontrolled exception type escapes the public verify() API, degrading error diagnostics and violating the method's declared exception contract.
validated_findings.impact: The unchecked RuntimeException propagates out of verify() uncaught, so callers (e.g. ThemeVerifierMojo) receive a raw RuntimeException/stack trace instead of the documented MojoExecutionException, breaking the expected error-handling contract of verify() and producing a less controlled build failure.
validated_findings.root_cause: New verifySafeHtml() method converts checked IOException into an unchecked RuntimeException instead of integrating with the existing checked-exception flow used by verify().
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Let verifySafeHtml() declare 'throws IOException' (or otherwise propagate the checked exception) so it is caught by the existing try/catch(IOException) in verify() and converted into a MojoExecutionException, consistent with verifyNoDuplicateKeys().
validated_findings.title: verifySafeHtml() wraps missing-file IOException as unchecked RuntimeException, bypassing verify()'s error handling contract
validated_findings.trigger: When either the target properties file or its derived English sibling file cannot be opened (e.g. missing/renamed English source file, permission issue) during verifySafeHtml(), which is invoked from verify() inside a try block that only catches checked IOException.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that RuntimeException bypasses verify()'s error handling is incorrect. Looking at verify() lines 46-55, the try-catch only wraps verifyNoDuplicateKeys() via Files.readString(), not verifySafeHtml(). verifySafeHtml() is called at line 51 outside the try block that catches IOException. The RuntimeException is intentional design for this private method, not a contract violation.

validated_findings.body: A regression that causes verifySafeHtml() to falsely flag legitimate translations (e.g. an identical anchor tag or an allowed element like <b>/<strong> matching the English source) as illegal HTML would not be caught by the current test suite, silently breaking valid theme builds.
validated_findings.failure_mode: False-positive regressions in the HTML sanitizer logic would go undetected by the test suite.
validated_findings.impact: A regression that causes verifySafeHtml() to falsely flag legitimate translations (e.g. an identical anchor tag or an allowed element like <b>/<strong> matching the English source) as illegal HTML would not be caught by the current test suite, silently breaking valid theme builds.
validated_findings.root_cause: New sanitizer test coverage only exercises the negative (violation-detected) branches of verifySafeHtml(), omitting the positive (no-violation) acceptance path.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a fixture pair (e.g. matching *_en.properties / *_xx.properties with identical allowed tags/anchors) and a test asserting VerifyMessageProperties.verify() returns an empty list for that case.
validated_findings.title: No positive-path test verifying that legitimate translations with matching allowed HTML pass without false-positive errors
validated_findings.trigger: All four newly added tests (verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected, verifyNoHtmlAllowed, verifyNoChangedAnchors, plus the duplicate-key test) only assert that an offending message IS produced; none assert that a valid translation reusing the same allowed elements/anchors as the English source produces an EMPTY message list.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage suggestion, not a defect introduced by the patch. The patch adds new negative-path tests which is valid. Absence of positive-path tests is a design choice, not a bug. The claim of 'false-positive regressions going undetected' is speculative without evidence of actual false positives.

validated_findings.body: The Lithuanian login theme displays an Italian sentence ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:') instead of a Lithuanian translation, confusing Lithuanian-speaking users during OTP setup.
validated_findings.evidence: loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:
validated_findings.failure_mode: Wrong-language UI text is shown to end users, degrading localization quality without any build/test failure to catch it.
validated_findings.impact: The Lithuanian login theme displays an Italian sentence ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:') instead of a Lithuanian translation, confusing Lithuanian-speaking users during OTP setup.
validated_findings.root_cause: Copy-paste from an Italian source string when updating the loginTotpStep1 message for the Lithuanian locale.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the value with a proper Lithuanian translation, e.g. 'Įdiekite vieną iš šių programų savo telefone:' matching the pattern used in other locales.
validated_findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 string replaced with untranslated Italian text
validated_findings.trigger: A Lithuanian-locale user reaches the Mobile Authenticator Setup (TOTP) screen during login.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at line 71 shows 'loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian text in the Lithuanian (messages_lt.properties) file. The repository context confirms this is Italian (matching messages_it.properties pattern). This is a clear copy-paste error introducing wrong-language text.
